newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia says expects to enter ASEAN in July.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia says expects to enter ASEAN in July.

text.p: Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas has told Cambodia's leaders that their country will be admitted to the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) in July, a top Cambodian official said on Tuesday.

"It is confirmed. We will be the ASEAN member by July," co-Minister of the Council of Ministers Sok An told reporters after a meeting with Alatas, Indonesian President Suharto and Cambodian co-Premiers Prince Norodom Ranariddh and Hun Sen.
Sok An said Alatas told the co-premiers the news while giving a briefing on last week's ASEAN-European Union meeting in Singapore.
Cambodia holds observer status in the seven-member grouping, which comprises Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
Sok An's announcement appeared to indicate that Laos and Burma would also be admitted in July, when the grouping celebrates its 30th anniversary.
ASEAN decided late last year to admit Cambodia, Laos and Burma simultaneously, but did not specify a timeframe.
Alatas later told reporters that Jakarta and other ASEAN nations wanted to see Cambodia join the regional body in July but would not confirm that it would be admitted this year.
"We hope that if the process is finalised before our July meeting of foreign ministers, that (membership of the three countries) can be realised.
"I cannot go ahead of the process," he said, adding that a formal decision must come from all ASEAN leaders.
Suharto, who last visited Cambodia in 1968, arrived here on Monday on the first stop of a tour of Cambodia, Laos and Burma.
When asked to confirm Sok An's announcement, co-Minister of the Council of Ministers Veng Sereyvuth told Reuters: "It is not wrong."

Some political analysts said there had been concerns that a rift over power-sharing between Ranariddh and Hun Sen, who formed an uneasy coalition after general elections in 1993, might delay the country's entry into ASEAN.
But Sok An said the co-premiers had emphasised the country's stability in the meeting with Suharto and Alatas.
Cambodia and Indonesia also strengthened ties by signing a trade pact and a memorandum of understanding on oil and gas exploration and production, officials said.
Sok An said the trade pact would boost Indonesian imports of Cambodian soya and rice and increase two-way trade, currently worth about $10 to $15 million each year.

The oil and gas agreement between Cambodia and Pertamina, Indonesia's state-owned oil and gas company, provides for the exchange of human resources and technical information, the Ministry of Industry said in a statement.
